v.why: Swapping a skip for a 3x3 conv on the direct input-output edge gave no gain or a loss, unlike swapping pool/none/1x1.
Going from a 1x1 conv to a 3x3 conv is a marginal upgrade compared with replacing skip or pool.
Restoring a missing output edge with a conv adds a lot of capacity and information flow.
Adding a conv on an empty edge gives consistent gains, while replacing an existing op gives little.
With edge 0 removed, edge 3 is the only path from input to output, so removing it disconnects the cell.
Without the direct edge 3, removing edge 5 leaves the output with few inputs and often disconnected.
When edge 5 is already absent, removing edge 4 strips most of the output's incoming paths.
Filling an empty edge with a conv helps, whereas replacing skip or 1x1 on that edge was neutral or harmful.
Replacing a learnable 3x3 conv on the output edge with a parameter-free skip loses capacity.
Upgrading a parameter-free skip on the input edge to a 3x3 conv gives a larger gain than from none, as in experiments 46 and 81.

raw:
These ten hypotheses are drawn from the 100 experiments and checked against how DAG cells and convolution ops behave. I ran no new experiments. The weakest are #1 and #10: #1 is inconsistent in sign on IN16 (experiment 88), and #10's margin over `none` is small.

1. Replacing a skip_connect on edge 3 with a 3x3 conv has a lower gain than replacing other ops. Experiments 28, 47 and 88 show it is the only context where the upgrade is neutral or negative.
2. Upgrading edge 0 to a 3x3 conv has a lower gain when edge 0 is already a 1x1 conv. Experiments 45 and 98 are about zero or negative, while replacing a skip or pool edge gives clear gains.
3. Setting edge 5 to a 3x3 conv has a higher gain when edge 5 was `none`. The output edge is restored, as in experiment 66.
4. Setting edge 4 to a 3x3 conv has a higher gain when edge 4 was `none`. Experiments 62, 76 and 86 are all positive on every dataset.
5. Removing edge 3 has a lower effect when edge 0 is `none`. The cell is then disconnected from the input, as in experiment 59.
6. Removing edge 5 has a lower effect when edge 3 is `none`. Experiments 39 and 63 show it cuts off the last route to the output.
7. Removing edge 4 has a lower effect when edge 5 is `none`. Experiment 68 shows a large drop when the output has almost no inputs left.
8. Setting edge 1 to a 3x3 conv has a higher gain when edge 1 was `none`. Experiments 26, 52 and 57 are positive, while replacing a skip or 1x1 edge is neutral or negative.
9. Changing edge 5 to skip_connect has a lower effect when edge 5 is a 3x3 conv. Experiments 30 and 74 lose capacity on the output edge.
10. Upgrading edge 0 to a 3x3 conv has a higher gain when edge 0 is a skip_connect than when it is `none`. Experiments 46 and 81 gain more than experiments 21, 56 and 91.
